# finitevolX

> Finite-volume operators on staggered Arakawa C-grids in JAX, for ocean and atmosphere models. Grids carry one ghost ring and a same-index staggering (T centres, U east faces, V north faces, X corners); on them sit raw stencils, difference / interpolation / divergence / vorticity operators, upwind / WENO / TVD advection, diffusion, Coriolis and momentum advection, land-sea masks with coastal stencil fallback, boundary conditions, energy and PV diagnostics, wind and drag forcing, spectral / capacitance / CG / multigrid Poisson and Helmholtz solvers, and SSP-RK, multistep, IMEX and diffrax time steppers, in 1-D, 2-D, 3-D, multilayer and on the sphere. Everything is an Equinox module or a pure function, so it runs under jit, vmap and grad. Use these instead of hand-writing shifted slices, ghost-cell fills, Poisson solvers and Runge–Kutta loops.

One package, `finitevolx` (import `finitevolx as fvx`), installed from GitHub: `uv add "finitevolx @ git+https://github.com/jejjohnson/finitevolX.git"` (uv also picks up the tags it pins for its git-only dependencies spectraldiffx and gaussx). Spectral transforms and solvers come from spectraldiffx and are re-exported; structured linear algebra comes from gaussx. Before writing a helper, search the capability index — every public name with a one-line summary, plus the spectraldiffx and gaussx APIs. Code you add should keep three rules:

- **The caller owns the ghost ring:** operators write only the interior `[1:-1, 1:-1]` and leave the ghosts zero; fill them (`fvx.enforce_periodic`, a `fvx.BoundaryConditionSet`, …) on every field before the next operator reads it, including inside a time stepper's right-hand side.
- **Use the operator that names the stagger:** `fvx.Difference2D(grid=grid).diff_x_T_to_U(h)`, `fvx.Interpolation2D(grid=grid).U_to_T(u)`, `fvx.Advection2D(grid=grid, mask=mask)(q, u, v, method="weno5")`, rather than writing the slice; pass a `fvx.Mask2D` as `mask=` so outputs are zero on land.
- **Units and JAX:** physical constants are overridable parameters, never baked into operators (so nondimensional models work); pure functions, no Python control flow on traced values, float32 in gives float32 out.

Claude Code users can install the `finitevolx` plugin: `/plugin marketplace add jejjohnson/finitevolX`, then `/plugin install finitevolx@finitevolx`.

## Start here

- [Home](https://jejjohnson.github.io/finitevolX/): what finitevolX is and a quick start
- [Capability index](https://jejjohnson.github.io/finitevolX/capabilities/): every public name, grouped by module, with a summary; then spectraldiffx and gaussx
- [Building with agents](https://jejjohnson.github.io/finitevolX/agents/): the Claude Code plugin, this file, and rules to paste into your project's AGENTS.md
- [C-grid discretization](https://jejjohnson.github.io/finitevolX/cgrid_discretization/): staggering, array shapes and the ghost-cell convention
- [Raw stencils](https://jejjohnson.github.io/finitevolX/stencils/): the finite-volume derivation and the three operator layers
- [Masks](https://jejjohnson.github.io/finitevolX/masks/): land-sea masks, staggered masks and coastal stencil fallback
